claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: regulator/label (live FDA label PDF, independent of the DailyMed page cited) plus NCBI Bookshelf/LiverTox structured database
claimVerdicts.finding: Core percentages (nausea 40%, hyperpigmentation 1%, RECONNECT AE rates) are independently confirmed (LiverTox: nausea 40%, flushing 20%, headache 11%, hyperpigmentation 'uncommon'). However the claim omits a safety-relevant nuance that the packet's own reviewFlag flagged for checking: the live FDA label states resolution of focal hyperpigmentation 'was not confirmed in all patients after discontinuation' and patient labeling states the darkening 'may not go away' -- i.e. it can be irreversible/permanent in some patients. claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: structured authority database / clinical reference (NCBI Bookshelf, LiverTox) — independent of DailyMed and DrugBank
claimVerdicts.finding: Independently confirmed: bremelanotide is a synthetic MSH-alpha analogue engaging melanocortin receptors, primarily MC4R (implicated in sexual desire) and MC1R (implicated in skin pigmentation, explaining the hyperpigmentation adverse effect). This resolves the packet's own reviewFlag about receptor-subtype specificity — recommend the claim explicitly name MC1R alongside MC4R, since MC1R engagement is the accepted mechanistic explanation for the hyperpigmentation AE documented elsewhere in the packet.

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: paper-level primary literature / independent reanalysis (Journal of Sex Research, Spielmans 2021) — independent of the original Kingsberg RCT report and the label
claimVerdicts.finding: The topline p-values and point estimates quoted are numerically confirmed. But an independent peer-reviewed reanalysis of the same RECONNECT trials found: (1) ~73% of protocol-prespecified outcomes were not reported in Kingsberg et al., with post-hoc secondary measures substituted; (2) only ~40.5% of bremelanotide-arm participants elected to continue into open-label extension versus ~69.4% of placebo-arm participants (patients net-preferred placebo, NNH~4); (3) dropout due to adverse events was about 12-fold higher on bremelanotide than placebo. The ICSM 2024 guideline separately notes bremelanotide 'did not affect the number of satisfying sexual events,' a patient-centered secondary measure. As currently worded the claim presents only the favorable co-primary endpoint results without this tolerability/preference context, which risks efficacy inflation beyond what the underlying data support for a fieldAuthorityRequired claim -- recommend adding a sentence on the discordant patient-preference/completion and AE-dropout data alongside the statistically significant co-primary results.

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: paper-level primary literature (PubMed) — independent of the vendor page and DailyMed label
claimVerdicts.finding: The reviewFlag states 'no controlled human trial for intranasal PT-141 was located' and the claim implies the intranasal route is wholly untested in humans. This is inaccurate: legitimate published controlled human trials of intranasal PT-141/bremelanotide do exist from the original (pre-Vyleesi) Palatin development program, e.g. Diamond et al., double-blind placebo-controlled dose/pharmacodynamic studies of intranasal PT-141 in men (including with sildenafil co-administration, PMID 15833522), and an early intranasal trial in women with arousal disorder (Safarinejad 2008) that was later formally RETRACTED (PMID 18179455) — itself worth noting as a specific misinformation-relevant caveat. The historical intranasal route was in fact where the drug's transient BP/HR signal was first characterized, which is part of why development shifted to the SC route used in Vyleesi. Recommend revising the claim to state that intranasal PT-141 was studied in early-phase trials (primarily in men, one relevant women's trial subsequently retracted) but that current unregulated compounded vendor products are unapproved, untested at their marketed concentrations, and not supported by the RECONNECT (SC) evidence -- rather than asserting no human data exists for the route at all.

Independently, maritimestudy.com (Amgen's dedicated MARITIME program site, a materially different source than the cited nct06858839 registry entry and amgen-story press page) confirms the Phase 3 structure described in the claim: MARITIME-1 (overweight/obesity) and MARITIME-2 (T2D) are 'Active, not recruiting,' with MARITIME-CV, MARITIME-HF, and MARITIME-OSA now actively recruiting — matching the claim's description of additional cardiovascular/heart-failure/OSA studies. The packet's own extensive documented search-and-gap process satisfies the directive's fallback rule (no independent regulator source exists; the gap is properly recorded, not glossed over).

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: professional clinical-news secondary reporting (independently corroborated by HCPLive)
claimVerdicts.finding: AJMC and HCPLive (independent professional medical-news sources, distinct from the cited PubMed abstract and Amgen PR) both report the identical ITT figures: obesity-only cohort -12.3% to -16.2% vs -2.5% placebo; obesity+T2D cohort -8.4% to -12.3% vs -1.7% placebo; HbA1c -1.2 to -1.6 points vs 0.1 placebo. All numbers in the claim check out exactly. Note: AJMC clarifies that the higher 'up to ~20%'/'up to 17%' figures (also cited from the Amgen PR in the packet's evidence) come from a separate 'efficacy estimand' (on-treatment, not intention-to-treat) — the packet blends both estimands in the same sentence/evidence list without explicitly flagging that the ITT and efficacy-estimand numbers are different endpoints; a brief clarifying phrase distinguishing 'treatment-policy/ITT' vs 'efficacy estimand' figures would remove any ambiguity, though nothing here is factually wrong or medical-advice-adjacent.

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: professional clinical-news secondary reporting (independent of cited PubMed + sponsor PR)
claimVerdicts.finding: AJMC and HCPLive independently confirm the 140/280/420 mg every-4-weeks and 420 mg every-8-weeks dosing arms with multiple dose-escalation schedules. Independent regulator check (FDA.gov/DailyMed, today) confirms no approved/labeled dose exists, matching the claim's explicit disclaimer language. Correctly kept fieldAuthorityRequired-gated and framed as protocol-only, not a use recommendation.

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: professional clinical-news secondary reporting (independent of cited PubMed + sponsor PR); cross-checked against Patient Care Online
claimVerdicts.finding: Safety-critical, checked first. AJMC independently reports 'dose escalation group GI-related discontinuation: 8%' and overall AE rate 93.5%, which corroborates the packet's '<8% GI-related' figure and the qualitative claim that GI events were the most common AE, milder/less frequent with dose escalation, and no unexpected safety signals emerged (also independently corroborated by Patient Care Online and the maritimestudy.com program page). Note: the packet's specific '~11% discontinuation due to any AE' figure traces only to the sponsor PR — no independent source I found restates that exact number verbatim (AJMC instead breaks discontinuation out by subgroup: 12%-17% in no-escalation arms), so that precise composite figure remains sponsor-sourced even though the directionally-consistent, more granular independent breakdown supports the same overall safety picture. Recommend citing the AJMC subgroup breakdown alongside the sponsor figure for a fully independent-sourced number, but nothing here overstates safety or reads as medical advice.

claimVerdicts.finding: Independent search today found no published MARITIME Phase 3 primary results; maritimestudy.com shows MARITIME-1/2 as 'Active, not recruiting' (ongoing, not completed/reported) and lists no results. This confirms the claim that human evidence remains limited to the single Phase 2 trial with no completed Phase 3, long-term, or cardiovascular/renal outcomes data yet.

notes: All 3 fieldAuthorityRequired claims (regulatory status, dose-context, adverse-effect/discontinuation) were independently re-verified against materially different source families (live FDA.gov/DailyMed regulator check, independent professional clinical-news reporting distinct from the cited PubMed+sponsor-PR pairing) and hold up.

The packet's own extensive, dated (2026-08-29) documentation of 'searched and not found' regulator sources for the regulatory/dose/adverse-effect claims exactly matches what my independent re-search today also found — no FDA, DailyMed, or EMA record exists for this compound. This is the correct honest outcome per the directive's fallback rule, not a gap that independent research could close.

One nuance worth recording: the efficacy claim mixes an intention-to-treat estimand (-12.3% to -16.2% / -8.4% to -12.3%) with an 'efficacy estimand' figure from the Amgen PR ('up to ~20%') in the same evidence bundle without labeling which is which; recommend a one-clause clarification distinguishing the two estimands.

The precise '~11% discontinuation due to any AE' figure in the adverse-effect claim remains sponsor-PR-only; independent sources corroborate the GI-specific <8% figure and the overall safety narrative but report discontinuation by different subgroup cuts (8% vs 12%-17%) rather than restating the exact composite number.

Live re-fetch of the vendor marketing page (meridianmedicalcentre.com) today confirms it is still active and still selling at $1,300 with 'Buy From The Official Website' language — the reviewFlags' warning that this content is volatile and needs reverification at review time was correctly flagged and today's recheck confirms it is unchanged.

The packet's ops.needsReview=true flag (human sign-off requirement for expansion-batch packets) is a workflow gate, not an evidence defect; independent verification found no needs-adjustment items, so from an evidence-quality standpoint the packet is ready, but the standard human sign-off step should still formally occur before publication.
